name: 读取情报（灯塔）板：有几条任务、各自什么状态
preconditions: reached Page.INTEL on the live client (proved by verify_open_intel, not by a remembered coordinate)
the board's own entry BTN_OPEN_INTEL_WILD_HUD present in the current frame (template lookup)
action-specific verifier exists before real try -- verify_open_intel / verify_intel_list_read

required_state.note: the board reads CLAIMABLE when at least one mission is finished and 一键领取 is drawn; it does not stop being a list of missions when it does

verification.reached_the_board: verify_open_intel(before = MAP frame, after = board frame) -> OK, live 2026-10-05T08:13Z and again at 08:17Z. This half is genuinely proven, twice.
verification.read_the_list: verify_intel_list_read -> ok=True on the 08:17Z capture (list_read=True, status=AVAILABLE) and ok=False on the 08:13Z capture (INTEL_LIST_UNKNOWN, because that reading carried no list_read). So the verifier is satisfiable, but only on the readings that happen to carry the count -- see failure_patterns[0].

success_condition_status.status_known: YES -- measured live twice: status=CLAIMABLE at 08:13Z and AVAILABLE at 08:17Z, and stamina read off the frame both times (35, then 13).
success_condition_status.count_known: PARTLY, AND UNRELIABLY. At 08:17Z the reading carried a real count (pins=9, available_count=9) that AGREED with the detector's 9. At 08:13Z the SAME page carried no count at all -- {status, claimable_count, stamina}, with claimable_count=1 counting ready rewards, not missions -- while the board drew 7 pins. The count field arrives and leaves depending on whether a reward is ready.
success_condition_status.honest_verdict: PARTIAL. This is a Step, not a complete Skill. Walking to the board and reading its state is proven live twice; the COUNT half of intel_count_and_status_known is carried on some frames and dropped on others, so the condition cannot be relied on as written.

spend: none -- reaching and reading the board costs nothing; no pin was tapped, no mission dispatched, no reward claimed. Dispatching costs stamina irreversibly and is EXECUTE_INTEL's job; claiming is CLAIM_INTEL_REWARDS'.
blocker: TWO measured defects, not one. (D1) The reading's SHAPE is unstable on the very page that carries the count: verify_intel_list_read requires intel['list_read'], and list_read appears ONLY on the frames where the pin counter also ran -- ocr.py:6116 gates that counter behind status == UNKNOWN, and the template layer answers CLAIMABLE before control reaches it. Measured on the same board four minutes apart: with a reward ready the reading was {status: CLAIMABLE, claimable_count: 1, stamina: 35} -- no count, no list_read -- while the board drew 7 pins; with nothing ready it was available_count=9, pins=9, list_read=True while the board drew 9 pins. (D2) The capability has never actually been executed: its ledger row under CLEAR_INTEL is 0 attempts / 0 successes / 0 failures, and the blocker's last_skill is OPEN_MAP -- an entry action, not a read. A first reading of this record claimed the verifier and the meter were mutually exclusive; a second live capture falsified that, because one frame did satisfy both. D1 is the measured cause; whether D1 explains D2 is a hypothesis, not a measurement.
verified_variant: board with 7 pins drawn, status=CLAIMABLE, claimable_count=1, stamina=35, 下次刷新 07:46:37, 一键领取 present; and four minutes later the same page with 9 pins, status=AVAILABLE, available_count=9, pins=9, list_read=True, stamina=13

failure_patterns.what: the same page produces two different reading SHAPES. The OCR branch that counts pins (ocr.py:6116-6120) runs only when intel['status'] is UNKNOWN, and it is the only thing that writes pins / available_count / list_read. The template layer answers CLAIMABLE first whenever a reward is ready (BTN_INTEL_CLAIM_ALL, vision.py:2288), so on exactly those frames control never reaches the counter and the reading degrades to {status, claimable_count, stamina}.
failure_patterns.measured: one board, four minutes apart, both captured live 2026-10-05. 08:13Z -- 一键领取 drawn, status=CLAIMABLE, reading carried NO available_count / NO pins / NO list_read, board drew 7 pins. 08:17Z -- nothing claimable, status=AVAILABLE, reading carried available_count=9 / pins=9 / list_read=True, board drew 9 pins. Both frames are the same page.
failure_patterns.why_it_has_not_bitten_yet: it has bitten: verify_intel_list_read keys on list_read, so the verifier is satisfiable only on the half of the readings that happens to carry the count. That is how an episode can pass its verifier while the goal has nothing to report.
failure_patterns.guard: tests/test_intel_list_reading.py asserts the two shapes separately -- the claimable board must carry no count and no list_read, and the non-claimable board must carry both.

failure_patterns.what: under CLEAR_INTEL the ledger row for READ_INTEL_LIST is 0 attempts / 0 successes / 0 failures, while the blocker's last_skill is OPEN_MAP and its failure_signature is 'READ_INTEL_LIST|NO_GOAL_PROGRESS|OPEN_MAP'. The episodes were spending themselves on ENTRY actions (going to the map, opening the page) rather than on a read.
failure_patterns.consequence: the target of this chain is not 'a read that failed' but 'a read that was never made'. Whether that is downstream of the unstable reading shape above is a HYPOTHESIS -- it is not measured, and it is recorded as such.

failure_patterns.what: the specific gate behind the pattern above: ocr.py:6116 runs _intel_pin_count only when the status is UNKNOWN. Measured over the intel corpus, TARGET_INTEL_BEAST_MISSION is the single most populated intel template (13 records: 10 + 3) and it sits ABOVE PAGE_INTEL -- the branch that yields status=UNKNOWN -- in vision.py's if-chain, so the counter is off precisely on the frames the template recognises best.

goal_library.py:1195-1196 emits CLEAR_INTEL whenever world.intel['status'] != 'UNKNOWN', with no test on world.page. A mission DIALOG frame carries intel={status: AVAILABLE, mission_type: HERO_JOURNEY, mission_level: 10} (vision.py:1734-1740) and therefore emits the goal -- on a frame where runtime.py:8994 can never stamp a meter, because page is POPUP and mission_type is set.
failure_patterns.measured: learning/goal_state.json CLEAR_INTEL carried exactly that reading while the runtime's own page was MAP: the goal's stored evidence came from a dialog frame, which is why its evidence dict has no untried_pins and its meter fell back to the constant distance 1.0.
failure_patterns.consequence: the goal spends part of its life on frames where it cannot report progress at all.

failure_patterns.what: community sources give 'about 10 stamina per mission' and one explicitly states that exact per-mission-type stamina costs are not officially documented. This client has four measured values instead (knowledge/game/intel.json, VERIFIED): 炽红巨兽 10, 营救幸存者 12, 英雄之旅 10, 大师悬赏 10.
failure_patterns.consequence: per the standing order 真机观察 > Episode > CONFIRMED > OBSERVED > 官方 > 社区 > 视频 > 模型推测, nothing from the community tables is written here as fact.
